title: Read only
summary: Read only is used when form data should be visible but not editable.
preamble: The read only allows users to review information in the same context and structure as editable form content, while making it clear that the value cannot be changed.

columns.content:
Use read only when:

- A value needs to remain visible as part of a form or form-like flow, but cannot be changed.
- Information has already been submitted or confirmed and should only be reviewed.
- A value is determined by another source, system or previous choice.
- Some fields in an otherwise editable form cannot be changed.

If the information is presented only for reading and is not part of a form context, consider using regular text or another content component instead.

columns.title: Read only
columns.content: Read only means that the value is available and relevant, it can receive focus but cannot be changed. The content should remain clearly readable and accessible.

columns.title: Disabled
columns.content: Disabled means that a control or action is currently unavailable. Disabled components may have reduced visual emphasis and are generally not interactive. Do not use a disabled state simply to prevent users from editing a value.

The read only treatment is consistent across form components, while adapting to the characteristics of each component.

- Keeps the value clearly visible and easy to read.
- Retains enough of the component's structure to make the relationship between label and value clear.
- Clearly differs from editable components without appearing disabled.
- Avoids visual cues that suggest the component can be interacted with.

Read only components:

- Cannot be changed by the user.
- Do not show hover, active or editable states.
- Should allow text content to be selected and copied where relevant.
- Should remain accessible to assistive technologies.
